doc.brief: Abort a blocking read operation running in a different thread.
details: The target read function returns immediately with ::cpp_core::StatusCode::Io::kAbortReadError.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Abort a blocking write operation running in a different thread.
details: The target write function returns immediately with ::cpp_core::StatusCode::Io::kAbortWriteError.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Clear (flush) the device's input buffer.
details: Discards every byte the driver has already received but the application has not yet read.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Clear (flush) the device's output buffer.
details: Blocks until all queued bytes have been transmitted and then discards any remaining data.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Close a previously opened serial port.
details: The handle becomes invalid after the call. Passing an already invalid (< = 0) handle is a no-op.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Query the current baud rate of an open serial port.
details: Reads back the baud rate that the OS driver is currently using. Useful for verifying that serialOpen() or serialSetBaudrate() applied the requested value.
doc.returns: Current baud rate in bit/s (>= 300) or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Read the current state of the Clear To Send (CTS) input line.
details: CTS is asserted by the remote device to indicate it is ready to receive data. Polling this line is useful when manual flow-control logic is required instead of (or in addition to) automatic RTS/CTS flow control.
doc.returns: 1 if asserted (HIGH), 0 if de-asserted (LOW), or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Query the current number of data bits of an open serial port.
doc.returns: Current data-bit setting. On error, the underlying integer value is a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Read the current state of the Data Carrier Detect (DCD) input line.
details: DCD is asserted by a modem when a carrier signal has been detected on the telephone line. For direct serial links it can serve as a general-purpose "connection alive"indicator.
doc.returns: 1 if asserted (HIGH), 0 if de-asserted (LOW), or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Read the current state of the Data Set Ready (DSR) input line.
details: DSR is asserted by the remote device to indicate it is powered on and ready to communicate. It is the counterpart to DTR.
doc.returns: 1 if asserted (HIGH), 0 if de-asserted (LOW), or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Query the current flow-control mode of an open serial port.
doc.returns: Current flow-control mode. On error, the underlying integer value is a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Query the current parity setting of an open serial port.
doc.returns: Current parity mode. On error, the underlying integer value is a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Read the current state of the Ring Indicator (RI) input line.
details: RI is asserted by a modem to signal an incoming call. On non-modem hardware it can be repurposed as a general-purpose input signal.
doc.returns: 1 if asserted (HIGH), 0 if de-asserted (LOW), or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Query the current stop-bit setting of an open serial port.
doc.returns: Current stop-bit setting. On error, the underlying integer value is a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Total number of bytes received since the port was opened.
doc.returns: Total number of bytes read or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Query how many bytes are immediately available to read.
details: The number reflects the size of the driver's RX FIFO **after** accounting for data already consumed by the application. A value of `0` therefore means a read call would have to wait for the next byte to arrive.
doc.returns: Bytes available for instant reading or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Enumerate all available serial ports on the system.
details: The supplied callback is invoked once for every discovered port. All string parameters may be `nullptr` if the information is unknown.
doc.returns: Number of ports found or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Open and configure a serial port.
details: The function attempts to open the device referenced by `port` and applies the line settings in `config`. `port` is interpreted as a UTF-8 encoded null-terminated string on all platforms.
doc.returns: A positive opaque handle on success or a negative value from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on failure.

doc.description: Null-terminated device identifier (e.g. "COM3", "/dev/ttyUSB0"). Passing `nullptr` results in a failure.
Serial line configuration. Includes baud rate, data bits, parity, stop bits, and flow-control mode. Passing `nullptr` results in a failure.
[optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Total number of bytes transmitted since the port was opened.
doc.returns: Total number of bytes written or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Return the number of bytes that have been accepted by the driver but not yet sent.
details: Useful for gauging transmission progress in the background or for pacing further writes to avoid unbounded buffering.
doc.returns: Bytes still waiting in the TX FIFO or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Read raw bytes from the serial port.
details: The call blocks for at most `timeout_config->timeout_ms` milliseconds while waiting for the FIRST byte. For every subsequent byte the individual timeout is calculated as `timeout_ms * multiplier` from `timeout_config`.
doc.returns: Bytes read (0 on timeout) or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: Timeout settings for this operation. Passing `nullptr` results in a failure.
[optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Read until a specific byte sequence appears.
details: Reads bytes using the same timeout semantics as serialRead() and stops as soon as `sequence` has been received. Sequences may contain zero bytes, and the complete terminator is included in the returned data.
doc.returns: Bytes read (including the terminator) or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: Timeout settings for this operation. Passing `nullptr` results in a failure.
[optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Send a break condition on the serial line.
details: A break is a sustained logic-LOW that lasts longer than a normal character frame. Many protocols rely on it:
- **DMX512**: A break of >= 88 us marks the start of a new frame. - **LIN bus**: The master starts each frame with a 13-bit break. - **MODBUS RTU**: Some implementations use break for frame sync.
The `duration_ms` parameter is a *minimum* - the actual break may be slightly longer due to OS scheduling.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Change the baud rate of an already-open serial port.
details: The new rate takes effect immediately without closing and re-opening the port. All other line settings (data bits, parity, stop bits, flow control) remain unchanged.
Typical use-case: a bootloader handshake starts at a safe 9600 baud and then both sides switch to a higher speed for the actual data transfer.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Change the number of data bits on an already-open serial port.
details: Takes effect immediately. All other line settings remain unchanged.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Set or clear the Data Terminal Ready (DTR) modem control line.
details: DTR is commonly used for: - Signalling readiness to the remote device. - Triggering a board reset on Arduino-compatible hardware. - Half-duplex direction control on RS-485 adapters.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: Non-zero to assert (HIGH), zero to de-assert (LOW).
[optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Register a callback that is invoked whenever an error occurs.
details: Pass `nullptr` to disable the callback.

doc.description: Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`. Gets invoked on any error.

doc.brief: Register or clear the serial-port lifecycle event callback.
details: Passing a non-null callback starts monitoring and invokes it with ::cpp_core::PortEvent::kAttached or ::cpp_core::PortEvent::kDetached. Passing `nullptr` clears the callback and stops monitoring.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: Notification callback or `nullptr` to stop monitoring.
[optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Configure the flow-control mode for an open serial port.
details: Flow control prevents buffer overruns when one side is slower than the other. Three modes are supported:

| `flow_mode` | Meaning | |------------------------------|----------------------------------------------| | `FlowControl::kNone` | No flow control. | | `FlowControl::kRtsCts` | Hardware RTS/CTS flow control. | | `FlowControl::kXonXoff` | Software XON/XOFF flow control. |
Changing the mode on an already-open port takes effect immediately.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Change the parity setting on an already-open serial port.
details: Takes effect immediately. All other line settings remain unchanged.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Register a callback that is invoked whenever bytes are read.
details: Pass `nullptr` to disable the callback.

doc.brief: Set or clear the Request To Send (RTS) modem control line.
details: RTS is typically used for hardware flow control (RTS/CTS) or as a transmit-enable signal in half-duplex RS-485 setups. When hardware flow control is **not** enabled via serialSetFlowControl(), this function gives manual control over the line.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: Non-zero to assert (HIGH), zero to de-assert (LOW).
[optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Change the stop-bit setting on an already-open serial port.
details: Takes effect immediately. All other line settings remain unchanged.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Register a callback that is invoked whenever bytes are written.
details: Pass `nullptr` to disable the callback.

doc.brief: Wait until the operating-system driver has physically sent every queued byte.
details: The function blocks the *calling thread* until the device driver reports that the transmit FIFO is **empty** - i.e. all bytes handed to previous `serialWrite*` calls have been shifted out on the wire. It does *not* flush higher-level protocol buffers you may have implemented yourself.
Typical use-case: ensure a complete command frame has left the UART before toggling RTS/DTR or powering down the device.
doc.returns: 0 on success or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: [optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.

doc.brief: Write raw bytes to the serial port.
details: Timeout handling mirrors serialRead(): `timeout_config->timeout_ms` applies to the first byte, `timeout_ms * multiplier` to every subsequent one.
doc.returns: Bytes written (may be 0 on timeout) or a negative error code from ::cpp_core::StatusCode on error.

doc.description: Timeout settings for this operation. Passing `nullptr` results in a failure.
[optional] Callback to invoke on error. Defined in error_callback.h. Default is `nullptr`.
